findings: The November 7, 2026 parent index links Checkout, Direct API, iOS and Android (new raw lines 5–17). It provides navigation for the same four routes inlined in the May 7, 2026 capture (old raw lines 18–35 and 63–82, 248–256, 632–637, 841–849). It provides no variant implementation or change to the payment model.

The May guide says activation automatically enables recurring payments for most users, subject to PayPal policy and regional or legacy-account restrictions. The manual Dashboard path goes pending and usually takes up to five business days; testing enables recurring by default (old raw lines 18–29). Checkout uses a Customer ID and a setup-mode Session. Retrieve the authorized payment method via the Session's SetupIntent and PaymentMethod ID, using a webhook or verified server retrieval when the buyer returns (old raw lines 49–183).

For May Direct API and mobile, the server creates a PayPal SetupIntent with customer_account (Accounts v2) or customer (Customers v1) and passes its client secret to the client. The web guide uses confirmPayPalSetup and a PayPal billing-agreement redirect, with a server-side requires_action / next_action.redirect_to_url alternative. iOS STPPaymentHandler.confirmSetupIntent and Android PaymentLauncher.confirm with ConfirmSetupIntentParams are separate historical SDK routes (old raw lines 285–386, 505–586, 652–733, 866–912 and 929–1018). Checkout's Session success_url differs from the Direct API setup return_url and the iOS sample return URL.

After successful buyer authorization Stripe emits setup_intent.succeeded; failure emits setup_intent.setup_failed and returns SetupIntent to requires_payment_method. The test steps discuss PaymentIntent outcomes separately. Later off-session charging creates and confirms a PaymentIntent using saved Customer/PaymentMethod IDs and errors if authentication is required. For Direct API on-session confirmation, return_url is conditionally optional with a PaymentMethod previously set up via SetupIntent or PaymentIntent setup_future_usage. For manual server-side on-session confirmation with a saved instrument, Fraudnet (web) or Magnes (mobile) supplies the required risk correlation ID, while Stripe.js has built-in Fraudnet. PayPal-side revocation emits mandate.updated, later charges fail using the saved instrument until it is replaced with one having an active mandate, and detach also revokes the Stripe mandate and calls PayPal to cancel the agreement (old raw lines 181–237, 384–503, 588–630, 1016–1061 and 1082–1124).

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paypal/set-up-future-payments, new raw lines 5–17 describe the guide's purpose and link Checkout, Direct API, iOS and Android. The merchant verifies successful authorization through setup_intent.succeeded, while failure emits setup_intent.setup_failed and returns requires_payment_method.
